question: Can the current saved eight-port fitting response recover internally equilibrated strip resultants and a nominal steel stress reference?
answer: Yes. The frozen operator's saved global q and loaded heel reproduce all saved eight-port and heel actions; the existing gross-rectangle section method then gives a conditional same-state nominal von Mises upper-bound / required-Fy reference. This does not establish product fitting strength.

reproduction.command: V10_ISOLATED_ROOT=/mnt/c/Users/mckay/Documents/Codex/2026-10-23/task-3/v10-isolated uv run python -B fea/generated/v10-packer-free-v1/connections/method-closure/fitting/gross-strip-current-v1/recover_gross_strip_sections.py --out <new ignored JSON path>
reproduction.method: For each of 24 descriptors per case, q is read at the exact 48 owned DOFs and converted from stored rotation scale; the saved heel-load shift is applied to the reconstructed rigid heel. The frozen `recover(full)` then rechecks energy, all eight signed port wrenches, strip-root actions and flange resultants. Each two-node strip span is cut at its ends; section force is constant and moment is linear without distributed span loads, so the existing pointwise gross-section bound is evaluated at endpoints.
reproduction.scope: Offline postprocessing of six saved fields. No candidate/global/native solve or CAD rebuild was run.

known_answer_control.basis: Single frozen Timoshenko gross-rectangle cantilever with signed tip N,V1,V2,T,M1,M2; direct statics recovers root and tip section resultants, and the existing rectangle stress bound matches the closed-form section envelope.

largest_reference_witness.location_scope: Ideal rigid heel section reference, not a measured formed-bend or flat-start section.

six_case_result.recovery_closure: For every fit in every case, the loaded heel, elastic energy, all signed port forces/couples, four strip-root wrenches, flange resultants and scaled gradient reproduce the saved action exactly. Span force equilibrium is exact; the maximum segment moment equilibrium residual is 1.1e-11 N·mm.

applicability_and_gaps.stress_result: The reported VM value is an upper-bound required-Fy reference for the declared ideal unperforated 44.45 x 6.35 mm gross half-strip under isotropic von Mises first yield. It is not a comparison against actual material Fy, not an ASD/LRFD capacity, and not a pass/fail acceptance.
applicability_and_gaps.holes_and_net_section: The elastic operator omits all eight factory holes. This report uses the full gross rectangle through hole planes; it does not model net-section strength, hole-edge concentration, bearing or tearout.
applicability_and_gaps.heel_and_plate: The four independent half-strips meet a rigid ideal heel. Plate-edge continuity, formed bend/radius compliance, short-connection restrained warping/bimoment, local force introduction and product thickness/tolerance are absent.
applicability_and_gaps.loads: The fitting body load is routed as a saved point wrench through the rigid heel. It is included in recovered actions but is not distributed along the strips as selfweight.
applicability_and_gaps.material_and_product: The frozen scenario has `steel_fy_mpa: null`; no actual product-specific yield strength, thickness or resistance is assigned.
applicability_and_gaps.prior_result_scope: Earlier `thin_bolted_steel_resistance` flange references use B103/B104 two-port layouts, 41.275 x 5.55625 mm legs, 14.2875 mm holes and different fitting/port counts. They do not describe this current eight-port operator. The current same-field report leaves angle/net-section/bend/fitting capacity null.
